owner_signature_observable.meaning: a valid on-chain ECDSA owner signature is observable after an executed UserOp

high_s_derivable.meaning: an observer can derive a high-s counterpart (s' = curve_order - s, v' = v XOR 1) recovering the identical signer

high_s_signature_length.meaning: byte length of the derived high-s raw ECDSA signature

signature_mismatch.meaning: the submitted high-s signature does not match the owner signature, i.e. signature validation fails
signature_mismatch.checkpoint: during validateUserOp of the griefing UserOp

returns_sig_validation_failed.checkpoint: during validateUserOp of the griefing UserOp

bundler_simulation_reverts.meaning: bundler simulation of the griefing UserOp reverts, wasting bundler compute on the submission
bundler_simulation_reverts.checkpoint: during bundler simulation of griefing UserOp

assumptions: The adversary is any observer of a valid owner signature; no specific caller authorization is required to submit griefing UserOps.
The griefing UserOp carries the derived high-s signature targeting an AtomWallet and is submitted to the EntryPoint.
Whether the bundler retries or blacklists is implementation-dependent; only the compute-waste revert is formalized here.

unresolved.description: Report describes the compute-waste effect as potential and does not establish an observed incident; the revert-on-simulation is treated as the observable outcome of the griefing submission.

limitations: Only the bundler_compute_waste impact is formalized; bundle_revert, gas_loss and wallet_degradation are handled in separate passes.
The high-s derivation relation (s' = curve_order - s, v' = v XOR 1) is represented as a grounded Boolean rather than an arithmetic identity because curve_order is not supplied as a literal.
